datasets.name: job_runs
datasets.query:
SELECT DISTINCT concat(date_format(run_started_at, 'MM-dd HH:mm'), ' ', replace(job_name, 'fraud-', '')) AS run_label,
       job_name,
       date_format(run_started_at, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') AS started,
       minutes_taken, CASE WHEN outcome IN ('SUCCEEDED', 'COMPLETED') THEN '✓ Succeeded' WHEN outcome IS NULL THEN '↻ Still running' ELSE concat('✕ ', initcap(replace(outcome, '_', ' '))) END AS outcome
FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times
ORDER BY started

datasets.name: newest_run
datasets.query:
SELECT DISTINCT date_format(run_started_at, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') AS started, minutes_taken, CASE WHEN outcome IN ('SUCCEEDED', 'COMPLETED') THEN '✓ Succeeded' WHEN outcome IS NULL THEN '↻ Still running' ELSE concat('✕ ', initcap(replace(outcome, '_', ' '))) END AS outcome
FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times
WHERE job_name = 'fraud-ingest'
  AND run_started_at = (SELECT MAX(run_started_at) FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times WHERE job_name = 'fraud-ingest')

datasets.name: task_times
datasets.query:
SELECT concat(date_format(run_started_at, 'MM-dd HH:mm'), ' ', replace(job_name, 'fraud-', '')) AS run_label, task_name, task_minutes
FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times
WHERE job_name = 'fraud-ingest' AND task_name IS NOT NULL

datasets.name: newest_run_tasks
datasets.query:
WITH tasks AS (SELECT task_name, task_minutes FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times
               WHERE job_name = 'fraud-ingest' AND task_name IS NOT NULL
                 AND run_started_at = (SELECT MAX(run_started_at) FROM workspace.fraud.job_run_times WHERE job_name = 'fraud-ingest'))
SELECT task_name, task_minutes,
       CASE WHEN task_minutes = MAX(task_minutes) OVER () THEN 'Slowest task' ELSE 'Other tasks' END AS task_kind
FROM tasks

datasets.name: pipeline_updates
datasets.query:
SELECT date_format(update_started_at, 'MM-dd HH:mm') AS update_label,
       minutes_taken, CASE WHEN outcome IN ('SUCCEEDED', 'COMPLETED') THEN '✓ Succeeded' WHEN outcome IS NULL THEN '↻ Still running' ELSE concat('✕ ', initcap(replace(outcome, '_', ' '))) END AS outcome,
       CASE WHEN full_rebuild THEN 'Full rebuild' ELSE 'New rows only' END AS update_kind
FROM workspace.fraud.pipeline_update_times
ORDER BY update_started_at

datasets.name: freshness
datasets.query:
WITH stages AS (
  SELECT '1. Copied to the landing folder' AS stage, newest_hour_released AS hour, newest_hour_released AS released FROM workspace.fraud.data_freshness
  UNION ALL SELECT '2. Loaded', newest_hour_ingested, newest_hour_released FROM workspace.fraud.data_freshness
  UNION ALL SELECT '3. Scored by the model', newest_hour_scored, newest_hour_released FROM workspace.fraud.data_freshness
  UNION ALL SELECT '4. Flagged for review', newest_hour_flagged, newest_hour_released FROM workspace.fraud.data_freshness)
SELECT stage, hour AS newest_simulated_hour, released - hour AS hours_behind,
       concat('Day ', CAST(floor((hour - 1) / 24) + 1 AS STRING), ', ', lpad(CAST((hour - 1) % 24 AS STRING), 2, '0'), ':00 (hour ', CAST(hour AS STRING), ')') AS newest_day_and_time,
       CASE WHEN released - hour = 0 THEN 'Up to date' ELSE 'Behind' END AS stage_status
FROM stages
ORDER BY stage

datasets.name: wait
datasets.query:
SELECT median_minutes_landing_to_scored AS typical_minutes,
       slowest_minutes_landing_to_scored AS longest_minutes
FROM workspace.fraud.data_freshness

datasets.name: rejections
datasets.query:
SELECT CASE reason WHEN 'missing_id' THEN 'Payment ID missing' WHEN 'missing_time' THEN 'Payment time missing' WHEN 'time_step_mismatch' THEN 'Payment time does not match its simulated hour' WHEN 'bad_amount' THEN 'Amount missing or below zero' WHEN 'unknown_type' THEN 'Unknown payment type' WHEN 'missing_account' THEN 'Account name missing' WHEN 'bad_label' THEN 'Fraud answer is not 0 or 1' WHEN 'unparsed_value' THEN 'A value could not be read' WHEN 'conflicting_duplicate' THEN 'Two different records with the same payment ID'
            ELSE reason END AS reason,
       rows_rejected, concat('Day ', CAST(floor((first_hour - 1) / 24) + 1 AS STRING), ', ', lpad(CAST((first_hour - 1) % 24 AS STRING), 2, '0'), ':00 (hour ', CAST(first_hour AS STRING), ')') AS first_day_and_time,
       concat('Day ', CAST(floor((last_hour - 1) / 24) + 1 AS STRING), ', ', lpad(CAST((last_hour - 1) % 24 AS STRING), 2, '0'), ':00 (hour ', CAST(last_hour AS STRING), ')') AS last_day_and_time
FROM workspace.fraud.rejected_rows_by_reason
ORDER BY rows_rejected DESC

widget.name: jobs_header
widget.textbox_spec:
## Are the jobs healthy?

Green runs succeeded, red ones need a look. Click a run or a legend entry to narrow the table below; right-click a run, then Drill to, to open it on the Run detail page.

frame.title: Newest fraud-ingest run
frame.description: How to read it: The loading job's latest run: when it started, how long it took and how it ended.

frame.title: Minutes per job run, oldest to newest
frame.description: How to read it: Each bar is one run, labelled with its start time and job. Taller means slower. Databricks records a run up to an hour after it ends, but the job refreshes this page as it ends, so its newest run is missing until you click Refresh an hour later.

frame.title: Where the time went in the newest run
frame.description: How to read it: Each bar is one task of the newest run; the slowest task is in full blue. The two dashboard refreshes run side by side, so the tasks can add up to more than the run.

frame.title: Minutes the cleaning pipeline itself spent per update
frame.description: How to read it: Compare with the silver task above: the difference is the time spent starting up and waiting, not cleaning.

frame.title: Every job run and how it ended
frame.description: How to read it: Anything other than ✓ Succeeded is a run that needs a look. Darker blue minutes are slower runs.

widget.name: data_header
widget.textbox_spec:
## Is the data fresh and clean?

After a run every stage should show the same simulated hour, and no rows should be set aside.

frame.title: Typical wait from landing to scored
frame.description: Latest scoring run only. Half of its payments waited less than this.

frame.title: Longest wait from landing to scored
frame.description: Latest scoring run only: the slowest payment.

frame.title: Newest simulated hour at each stage
frame.description: How to read it: Each bar is one stage, in pipeline order. Green stages are up to date; a red, shorter bar shows where payments are stuck. Hour 480 is day 20, 11 pm; each day has 24 hours.

frame.title: Hours behind the landing folder
frame.description: How to read it: 0 on a green cell means the stage has caught up; a red cell shows how many hours it lags.

frame.title: Rows set aside, by reason
frame.description: How to read it: Each row is one reason a payment record failed a basic check. Set-aside rows are kept for checking, never scored.

widget.name: detail_header
widget.textbox_spec:
## Run detail

Pick a run, or open one from a run's bar on the first page: right-click, then Drill to.

frame.title: The picked run
frame.description: How to read it: One row for the picked run; every run while none is picked.

frame.title: Where the time went in this run
frame.description: How to read it: Each bar is one task of the picked run; the longest bar is where the time went. With no run picked it shows each task's average over all runs. Only fraud-ingest runs record their tasks here, so a fraud-train run shows no bars.

widget.name: word_list
widget.textbox_spec:
# What these words mean

- **Flagged payment**: A payment the model ranked among the 50 most suspicious of its hour, so a person should look at it.
- **Case**: The review of one flagged payment. It stays open until its verdict is recorded.
- **Verdict**: The answer to a case: confirmed fraud or false alarm. It arrives 3 simulated days after the payment.
- **Confirmed fraud**: A flagged payment that really was fraud.
- **False alarm**: A flagged payment that turned out to be honest.
- **Simulated hour**: One hour of the replayed month of payments, numbered from 1 to 743. Hour 1 is day 1, midnight to 1 am; hour 480 is day 20, 11 pm.
- **Model version**: Which saved copy of the fraud model made the decision. Each new copy gets the next number.
- **Champion model**: The model version currently trusted to score new payments.
- **Risk score**: How suspicious the model found a payment. Higher is more suspicious. It ranks payments, it is not a chance.
- **Rejected row**: A payment record that failed a basic check, such as an amount below zero, and was set aside.
- **Job run**: One run of the scheduled work that releases, loads, cleans, scores and flags payments.
- **Task**: One step inside a job run, such as loading or scoring.
- **REDACTED**: Shown instead of an account name to people who may not see who paid whom.
- **Landing folder**: Where each simulated hour's file of payments arrives before it is loaded.
- **Pipeline update**: One run of the cleaning step that turns loaded payments into clean ones.
- **Full rebuild**: A pipeline update that redoes everything from the start instead of only the new rows.
- **Run detail**: A page showing one job run task by task. Open it from a run's bar: right-click, then Drill to.
